title: Client Services Desk Reference: Raising the Invoice for a Served Catering Order
content:
## When this applies

A catering order served under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement falls to be billed to the client. The result this governs is the amount invoiced for that single order, in USD.

## What the desk does

The desk raises the invoice for that one order on the client's agreement. Once it is raised, an invoice entry stands in the agreement's order history against that order reference, carrying the amount billed and the service day it covers, and the agreement's unsettled catering balance stands higher by that same amount. The client sees the order on their next statement as an invoice awaiting payment.

## Invoking the tool

The tool is `raise_catering_invoice_cb57dc9d`. It is an agent-side tool: the desk unlocks it and then calls it, one call per order billed.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catering_agreement_id` | the reference number of the corporate catering service agreement being billed | an identifier, as returned by the catering agreement lookup |
| `customer_id` | the reference number of the client organisation profile the agreement belongs to | an identifier, as returned by the dining profile lookup |
| `order_reference` | the catering order being billed, written as the order reference it carries throughout its history | CO- followed by 6 digits |
| `service_date` | the day the catering was served, in the site's own calendar | YYYY-MM-DD; never left empty |
| `invoice_amount_usd` | the amount billed for this order | USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half to even at the point it is booked and never carried to a finer precision; no time zone applies and it is never left empty |

## What comes back

A confirmation sentence naming the invoice number the entry was filed under, the order reference billed and the amount booked in USD to two decimal places. The presence of the invoice number in the sentence is what indicates the invoice was raised; afterwards the order history shows one further invoice entry and the agreement's unsettled catering balance stands higher by the amount booked.

## Contract Q&A

*Does one call cover more than one order?* No. One call raises the invoice for that single order, against the order reference given.

*What does the day given as the service day record?* The day the catering was served, which the entry carries as the day the invoice covers.
